text:
Maria L: Hey team — quick question about benefits changes. My spouse got coverage through their new job and we want to remove them from my health + dental midyear. How does that affect payroll deductions? Are we due a refund or is it prorated going forward?

Julia (People Ops): Congrats to your spouse! :partyparrot: Short answer: depends on the effective date and whether this counts as a QLE (qualifying life event). If you provide proof of new employer coverage within 31 days, we can process a midyear change. Deductions are typically prorated from the effective date forward; refunds for prior payroll periods are rare but possible in limited cases.

Maria L: Got it — what counts as proof? and what's the effective date — the spouse's coverage started on 3/1 but their HR didn't give us a formal letter until 3/10.

Julia (People Ops): We accept one of the following: enrollment confirmation email from their employer, benefits portal screenshot that shows active coverage and effective date, or an employer-signed letter. The effective date we use is the coverage start date on their employer document (so 3/1 in your example). Please upload docs to the Benefits portal and pick "Remove dependent - QLE".

Maria L: Thanks — can you confirm payroll timing? My paycheck cycles are 1st and 15th. If we submit docs this week, when would deductions change?

Kevin - Payroll: Hi Maria — payroll cutoffs matter. If docs and the People Ops approval hit us before the payroll cutoff for the 4/1 cycle (cutoff is 3/23 5pm PT), we can stop deductions starting 4/1. Per-policy, deductions already taken for pay periods before 4/1 are not automatically refunded unless there was an overpayment error.

Maria L: So no retro refund for March even though spouse coverage started 3/1? That feels rough.

Julia (People Ops): I understand. We can request a manual review if the proof shows spouse had other active coverage on 3/1 and you weren't eligible to cover them after that date. Manual refunds are evaluated case-by-case and require manager sign-off plus verification from the carrier. It helps to upload the earliest possible proof (the 3/1 doc).

Maria L: Okay i'll upload the portal screenshot now. One more Q: can we drop them from health but keep dental?

Julia (People Ops): Yes, you can elect to remove dependent from select plans. On the benefits change form choose which plans to update. Example snippet of what to select in the portal: 

```
Event type: Qualifying Life Event (QLE)
QLE reason: Spouse gained employer coverage
Effective date: 2025-03-01
Affected plans: Health: Remove dependent, Dental: Keep dependent (No change)
Attachments: Enrollment confirmation from spouse's employer
```

Maria L: Perfect. Upload done. Anything else I should tag?

Julia (People Ops): Nope, we have it. I flagged the case and submitted to benefits carrier for effective date verification. If everything matches we will send the change to payroll. Expect an update here within 5 business days.

HR Bot: Case #BEN-2025-914 created and assigned to Julia (People Ops). Please allow 3-5 business days for carrier verification.

Kevin - Payroll: Once People Ops approves, I'll post here when payroll actions are queued. If approved after the 3/23 cutoff we'll apply changes to the 4/15 cycle (deductions stop 4/15).

Maria L: Thank you both! Really appreciate the help. :heart:
